title: COVID-19 Vaccination Responses with Different Vaccine Platforms in Patients with Inborn Errors of Immunity.
ehr_evidence: Blood samples from patients and healthy adult donors were collected prior to vaccination (T0), 28 days (+ / − 3 days) after the first (T1) and the second (T2) doses.
summary: Observational study evaluating the safety and immunogenicity (humoral and cellular responses) of different COVID-19 vaccine platforms in patients with inborn errors of immunity and healthy controls in Argentina.
key_findings: No moderate or severe adverse events were observed in IEI patients following vaccination.
Anti-S/RBD IgG titers were significantly lower in IEI patients compared to healthy controls (p < 0.05 for adults, p < 0.005 for pediatrics).
Neutralizing antibody IC80 titers were significantly lower in IEI patients than in healthy controls (p < 0.01 for pediatrics, p < 0.05 for adults).
Positive S-specific IFN-γ response was observed in 84.5% of IEI patients, and 82.1% presented S-specific TFH cells.
Moderna vaccines elicited significantly stronger humoral responses and neutralization capacity compared to other platforms (p < 0.01 and p < 0.005, respectively).
No significant difference in humoral response was observed between vaccinated patients with or without previous SARS-CoV-2 infection.
captured_features: IgG anti-S/RBD and anti-N antibodies by ELISA
Neutralizing antibody IC50/IC80 via pseudo-virus assay
S-specific circulating TFH cell frequency by flow cytometry
population: 118 patients with inborn errors of immunity (79 adults aged 19-78, 39 pediatrics aged 12-18) and 37 age-matched healthy controls in Argentina
exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (mRNA, adenoviral vector, inactivated platforms)
limitations: Small sample size for specific IEI subtypes
Lack of long-term follow-up for immunogenicity
Limited PBMC samples for healthy pediatric controls prevented cellular response comparison
data_availability_statement: All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this published article (and its supplementary information files).
